recipes.title: Tomato Basil Pasta
recipes.tagline: A 30-minute weeknight pasta built on a fresh tomato sauce.
recipes.description: Ripe tomatoes cooked down with garlic and olive oil until they collapse into a sauce, finished with torn basil and starchy pasta water. One pan, one pot, no specialty shopping.

items.item: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and salt it until it tastes seasoned.
steps.tip: Under-salted water is the most common reason a finished pasta tastes flat.

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat, add the garlic, and cook until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the tomatoes and chilli flakes, raise the heat, and cook until the tomatoes collapse and the sauce thickens.
Cook the spaghetti one minute short of the package time, reserving a mug of the cooking water before draining.
Toss the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of the reserved water and stir hard until the sauce coats every strand.
steps.tip: The starch in the water is what emulsifies the sauce -- plain water will not do it.

steps.text: Kill the heat, fold in the torn basil, taste for salt, and serve with the Parmesan.

notes: Out of season, 2 x 400g tins of good whole plum tomatoes beat fresh ones.
Keeps 3 days refrigerated; loosen with a splash of water when reheating.

image.caption: Best served the moment the pasta hits the sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken Curry
recipes.tagline: A one-pot chicken curry with a spice base you can adjust to taste.
recipes.description: Onions cooked down until golden, bloomed with curry powder and ginger, then simmered with chicken thighs in coconut milk until the sauce clings. Mild for family dinners, hot if you want it.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onions until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder and cook briefly to toast the spices.
steps.tip: Toasting the spice in the fat before adding liquid wakes up flavour that a wet pan can't.

steps.text: Add the chicken pieces and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides.
Pour in the coconut milk, add salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Taste and adjust salt or spice, then garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.

notes: Swap thighs for a firm white fish in the last 8 minutes for a quicker version.
Keeps 3 days refrigerated, and freezes well for up to 2 months.

image.caption: Serve over steamed rice or with warm flatbread.

recipes.title: Classic Shakshuka
recipes.tagline: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, one skillet start to finish.
recipes.description: A North African and Eastern Mediterranean breakfast of eggs gently poached in a thick, cumin-scented tomato and pepper sauce. Scoop it up with warm bread straight from the pan.
equipment: Wide oven-safe skillet with a lid

items.item: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli flakes, and cook briefly until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer until thickened.
steps.tip: The sauce should hold its shape on a spoon before the eggs go in, or they'll swim instead of poach.

steps.text: Make small wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack an egg into each one.
Cover and cook over low heat until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Scatter with parsley and feta if using, and serve straight from the pan with warm bread.

notes: For a firmer yolk, extend the covered cooking time by 2 minutes.
The sauce alone keeps 3 days refrigerated -- make it ahead and poach eggs fresh to order.

recipes.title: Classic Pancakes
recipes.tagline: Fluffy stovetop pancakes with crisp edges and a tender crumb.
recipes.description: A basic buttermilk batter whisked together in one bowl and cooked in batches until golden -- the weekend breakfast that needs no special equipment.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just combined.
steps.tip: A few lumps are fine -- overmixing is what makes pancakes tough instead of fluffy.

steps.text: Let the batter rest while a skillet or griddle heats over medium heat.
Melt a little butter in the skillet, then ladle in batter for each pancake.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip and cook until golden on the other side.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve warm with maple syrup.

notes: Batter keeps refrigerated for 1 day -- expect it to thicken slightly overnight.
Stir in blueberries or chocolate chips just before cooking, if using.

image.caption: Stack them tall and serve while the top layer is still warm.

recipes.title: French Toast
recipes.tagline: Thick bread soaked in a cinnamon custard and pan-fried until golden.
recipes.description: Day-old bread soaked in an egg and milk custard, then fried in butter until crisp outside and custardy within -- the best use for slightly stale bread.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt together in a shallow dish.
Soak each bread slice for 20-30 seconds per side, until saturated but not falling apart.
steps.tip: Slightly stale bread soaks up the custard without turning to mush -- fresh bread works too, just soak it more briefly.

steps.text: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the soaked slices until golden on both sides.
Serve immediately with maple syrup and berries.

notes: A stale baguette or brioche loaf both work well here.
Keep finished slices warm in a low oven while frying the rest in batches.

recipes.title: Cheese Omelette
recipes.tagline: A folded egg omelette with melted cheese, ready in five minutes.
recipes.description: Whisked eggs cooked low and slow until just set, filled with melted cheese and folded -- a fast, protein-heavy breakfast that needs no fillers.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt, and pepper until fully combined.
Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat.
Pour in the eggs, let them sit undisturbed a few seconds, then gently push the cooked edges toward the center.
steps.tip: Low heat is what keeps an omelette tender -- high heat turns the eggs rubbery.

steps.text: When mostly set but still slightly wet on top, scatter the cheese over one half.
Fold the omelette over the cheese and slide it onto a plate.

notes: Swap the cheese for any melty variety, or add cooked vegetables before folding.
Three eggs makes a substantial single serving -- halve it for a lighter breakfast.

recipes.title: Belgian Waffles
recipes.tagline: Deep-pocketed waffles with a crisp crust and airy interior.
recipes.description: A batter lightened with whipped egg whites, cooked in a waffle iron until deeply golden -- crisp enough to hold a pool of syrup in every pocket.

items.item: butter and maple syrup, to serve

steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and whisk until just smooth.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold them into the batter.
steps.tip: Folding rather than stirring keeps the air in the whites, which is what gives the waffle its lift.

steps.text: Preheat the waffle iron and cook the batter in batches until deeply golden and crisp.
Serve immediately with butter and maple syrup.

notes: The batter deflates if left standing -- cook it soon after folding in the egg whites.
Leftover waffles freeze well and reheat directly in a toaster.

recipes.title: Classic Bruschetta
recipes.tagline: Grilled bread rubbed with garlic and piled with fresh tomatoes and basil.
recipes.description: Toasted bread brushed with olive oil, rubbed with raw garlic, and topped with a quick tomato-basil mixture -- ready in the time it takes to toast the bread.

steps.text: Brush the bread slices with olive oil and toast or grill until golden on both sides.
While still warm, rub each slice with the cut side of a garlic clove.
steps.tip: Rubbing raw garlic onto warm toast releases just enough bite without overwhelming the topping.

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, shallot, basil, olive oil, and balsamic vinegar in a bowl, and season with salt and pepper.
Let the tomato mixture sit for a few minutes to release its juices.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toasted bread just before serving.

notes: Assemble just before serving, or the bread turns soggy.
Salt the tomatoes only right before topping, not while they sit.

recipes.title: Classic Hummus
recipes.tagline: Creamy chickpea and tahini dip, blended smooth in minutes.
recipes.description: Chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic until silky -- better than store-bought and ready faster than a trip to buy it.

steps.text: Combine the chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and salt in a food processor.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, add reserved chickpea liquid a tablespoon at a time until silky.
steps.tip: The starchy liquid from the can is what gives hummus its light, whipped texture -- plain water works too, but not as well.

steps.text: Taste and adjust the salt or lemon.
Spread onto a plate, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with paprika and parsley before serving.

notes: Keeps 4 days refrigerated in a sealed container.
Flavor improves if it sits at room temperature for an hour before serving.

recipes.title: Vegetable Spring Rolls
recipes.tagline: Crisp fried rolls packed with shredded vegetables.
recipes.description: A shredded vegetable filling wrapped tight in spring roll pastry and fried until crackling -- a party appetizer worth the extra folding.

items.item: sweet chili sauce or soy dipping sauce

steps.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic until fragrant.
Add the cabbage, carrot, and bean sprouts, and stir-fry until just softened.
Stir in the spring onions, soy sauce, and sesame oil, then remove from heat and let cool completely.
steps.tip: A hot filling steams the wrapper and makes it tear -- let it cool before wrapping.

steps.text: Spoon filling onto a wrapper, fold the bottom corner over, tuck in the sides, and roll tightly, sealing the edge with a little water.
Heat oil to 175C (350F) and fry the rolls in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with dipping sauce.

notes: Rolls can be assembled ahead and refrigerated -- fry just before serving for maximum crunch.
Baking at 200C (400F) for 20 minutes, turning once, works as a lighter alternative to frying.

recipes.title: Fresh Guacamole
recipes.tagline: Mashed avocado brightened with lime, onion, and cilantro.
recipes.description: Ripe avocados mashed to a chunky puree with lime juice, onion, and chile -- the dip that disappears faster than you can make it.

steps.text: Halve the avocados, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash with a fork to your preferred chunkiness -- some smooth, some in pieces.
steps.tip: Mashing by hand instead of blending is what keeps guacamole from turning into paste.

steps.text: Stir in the lime juice, onion, jalapeno, cilantro, tomato, and salt.
Taste and adjust the salt or lime.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

notes: Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to slow browning if not serving right away.
A reserved avocado pit nestled in the bowl helps too, though the plastic wrap does more of the work.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Dumplings
recipes.tagline: Pork and cabbage dumplings, steamed then crisped in the pan.
recipes.description: A juicy pork and cabbage filling folded into wrappers, steamed until cooked through, then finished in a hot pan for a crisp golden base.

items.item: soy sauce and chili oil, for dipping

steps.text: Squeeze the salted cabbage to remove excess water, then combine with the pork, spring onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt.
steps.tip: Salting and squeezing the cabbage first keeps the filling from turning watery once it cooks.

steps.text: Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each wrapper, moisten the edge with water, and pleat closed.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and arrange the dumplings flat-side down.
Fry until the bottoms are golden.
Add the water, cover immediately, and steam until the filling is cooked through.
Uncover and let any remaining water evaporate so the bottoms re-crisp.
Serve hot with soy sauce and chili oil.

notes: Uncooked dumplings freeze well laid flat on a tray before being bagged.
Cook straight from frozen, adding about 2 extra minutes to the steaming step.

recipes.title: Beef Stroganoff
recipes.tagline: Seared beef and mushrooms in a creamy paprika-flecked sauce, over noodles.
recipes.description: Strips of beef seared hot and fast, then simmered briefly with mushrooms, onion, and a sour cream sauce -- classic comfort food over buttered egg noodles.

items.item: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned but not cooked through, then remove and set aside.
steps.tip: Crowding the pan steams the beef instead of browning it -- work in batches.

steps.text: Add the onion and mushrooms to the same skillet and cook until softened and golden.
Add the butter and flour, stirring to coat the vegetables, and cook for a minute to remove the raw flour taste.
Gradually whisk in the beef stock, then add the mustard, and simmer until slightly thickened.
Stir in the sour cream and return the beef to the pan, warming through without letting it boil.
steps.tip: Boiling after the sour cream goes in can make the sauce split.

steps.text: Taste and adjust salt and pepper, then serve over the egg noodles with parsley.

notes: Creme fraiche makes a slightly less tangy sauce than sour cream, if you prefer.
Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated but reheat gently to avoid splitting the sauce.

recipes.title: Spaghetti Carbonara
recipes.tagline: Pasta tossed in a silky egg and pecorino sauce with crisp pancetta.
recipes.description: Just five ingredients -- eggs, cheese, pancetta, pepper, and pasta -- combined off the heat so the eggs turn into a glossy sauce instead of scrambling.

items.note: finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
While the pasta cooks, fry the pancetta in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp and golden.
Whisk the whole eggs, egg yolks, pecorino, and a generous amount of black pepper together in a bowl.
Reserve a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta and add it to the skillet with the pancetta, off the heat.
Pour in the egg mixture, tossing constantly and adding splashes of the reserved pasta water until the sauce turns glossy and coats the pasta.
steps.tip: The pan must be off the heat when the eggs go in -- direct heat scrambles them instead of turning them into sauce.

steps.text: Serve immediately with extra pecorino and black pepper.

notes: Guanciale is the traditional cut if you can find it -- pancetta is a widely available substitute.
Heavy cream is not part of a traditional carbonara -- the emulsified eggs are what make the sauce silky.

image.caption: Serve the moment the sauce comes together -- it tightens as it cools.

recipes.title: Classic Lasagna
recipes.tagline: Layered pasta baked with a slow-simmered meat sauce and bechamel.
recipes.description: Sheets of pasta layered with a long-simmered beef and tomato sauce and a creamy bechamel, baked until bubbling and golden on top.

items.item: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic and ground beef, and cook until the beef is browned.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, salt, and pepper, and simmer uncovered until thickened.
steps.tip: The longer, slower simmer is what makes a meat sauce taste developed instead of just cooked -- do not rush this step.

steps.text: Meanwhile, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook for a minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened, then season with nutmeg and salt.
Preheat the oven to 190C (375F). Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in the baking dish, then layer pasta sheets, meat sauce, and bechamel, repeating to use it all up, finishing with bechamel.
Scatter the mozzarella and Parmesan over the top.
Bake until bubbling and golden on top.
Let it rest before slicing.
steps.tip: Slicing straight from the oven collapses the layers -- resting lets the lasagna set.

notes: Assembled, unbaked lasagna freezes well for up to 3 months -- thaw overnight before baking.
Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated and reheat well covered in a low oven.

image.alt: Slice of baked lasagna showing layers of pasta, meat sauce, and cheese
image.caption: Let it rest 15 minutes before cutting so the layers hold their shape.

recipes.title: Baked Mac and Cheese
recipes.tagline: Elbow pasta in a rich three-cheese sauce, baked until bubbling.
recipes.description: A roux-based cheese sauce coats tender pasta, topped with extra cheese and baked until the top turns golden and the edges go crisp.

steps.text: Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour, and cook a minute to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until thickened.
steps.tip: Adding the milk gradually while whisking is what keeps the sauce smooth instead of lumpy.

steps.text: Remove from heat and stir in the cheddar, gruyere, and mustard powder until melted, then season with salt and pepper.
Combine the sauce with the cooked macaroni and pour into a baking dish.
Scatter breadcrumbs and extra cheddar over the top, then bake until golden and bubbling.
Let it rest a few minutes before serving.

notes: Swap in any melty cheese combination -- a sharp cheddar plus something meltier like gruyere or gouda balances flavor and texture.
Keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered with a splash of milk stirred in.

recipes.title: Crispy Falafel
recipes.tagline: Herbed chickpea patties, fried until deeply golden and crisp.
recipes.description: Dried chickpeas soaked and blitzed with herbs and spices, then fried until the outside shatters and the inside stays tender.

items.note: soaked overnight and drained, not canned

steps.text: Combine the soaked chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, and coriander in a food processor.
steps.tip: Dried, soaked chickpeas hold together when fried -- canned chickpeas are too wet and the falafel falls apart in the oil.

steps.text: Pulse until finely chopped but not pureed -- the mixture should look like coarse sand, not paste.
Transfer to a bowl, stir in the baking powder, salt, and pepper, and refrigerate.
Shape the mixture into small balls or patties.
Heat oil to 175C (350F) and fry the falafel in batches until deeply golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm in pita with tahini sauce and vegetables.

notes: The overnight soak is essential -- dried chickpeas need at least 12 hours in water before blending.
Baked falafel (200C/400F for 25 minutes) works as a lighter alternative but loses some crispness.

recipes.title: Vegetable Fried Rice
recipes.tagline: Day-old rice stir-fried with egg and vegetables in a hot wok.
recipes.description: Cold, day-old rice separates into distinct grains in a hot wok, tossed with egg and whatever vegetables are on hand -- one of the fastest ways to turn leftovers into dinner.

steps.text: Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat, pour in the eggs, and scramble until just set, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic, carrot, and peas, and stir-fry until the carrot softens.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until heated through and starting to crisp in spots.
steps.tip: Cold, day-old rice fries up dry and separate -- fresh warm rice turns gluey in the wok.

steps.text: Return the scrambled egg to the wok, add the spring onions, soy sauce, and sesame oil, and toss to combine.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

notes: Freeze leftover rice in flat bags specifically for this -- it thaws and fries better than rice that's just been refrigerated a day.
Add any leftover cooked vegetables or protein along with the peas and carrot.

recipes.title: Greek Salad
recipes.tagline: Crisp vegetables and briny feta tossed in a simple oregano vinaigrette.
recipes.description: Tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and a thick slab of feta tossed with red onion and a sharp oregano dressing -- no lettuce, and none needed.

steps.text: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper together in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently.
Top with the feta, left as a slab or cubed and scattered over.
steps.tip: A slab of feta left whole on top, drizzled with oil and oregano, is the traditional presentation -- crumbling it is common but not classic.

steps.text: Serve immediately.

notes: Salt the tomatoes lightly and let them sit a few minutes first if they need extra flavor.
This salad does not keep well once dressed -- dress only what you'll eat that sitting.

recipes.title: Mushroom Risotto
recipes.tagline: Arborio rice stirred slowly with stock until creamy, folded with mushrooms.
recipes.description: Rice released of its starch one ladle of stock at a time, finished with sauteed mushrooms and Parmesan -- patience is the only hard part.

steps.text: Heat half the olive oil in a wide pan and saute the mushrooms until golden, then remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and cook the onion until softened.
Add the rice and stir for a minute until the grains are coated and glossy.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently and waiting until each addition is absorbed before adding the next.
steps.tip: Adding stock gradually and stirring often is what coaxes the starch out of the rice -- dump it all in at once and you get boiled rice, not risotto.

steps.text: When the rice is tender and creamy, stir in the butter, Parmesan, and reserved mushrooms.
Season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately with parsley and extra Parmesan.

notes: Risotto does not wait -- have your other courses ready before you start stirring.
Leftover risotto makes excellent fried arancini the next day.

recipes.title: Classic Tiramisu
recipes.tagline: Coffee-soaked ladyfingers layered with a mascarpone cream, no baking required.
recipes.description: Espresso-dunked ladyfingers layered with a whipped egg and mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoa and chilled until set -- the classic no-bake Italian dessert.

steps.text: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together until pale and thick.
Beat in the mascarpone until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip the heavy cream to soft peaks, then fold into the mascarpone mixture.
steps.tip: Folding rather than stirring keeps the cream light -- overmixing deflates it and the tiramisu ends up dense instead of airy.

steps.text: Combine the espresso and coffee liqueur in a shallow dish. Dip each ladyfinger briefly and arrange in a single layer in the baking dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with a second layer of dipped ladyfingers and the remaining cream.
Cover and refrigerate until set.
Dust with cocoa powder just before serving.

notes: Dip the ladyfingers quickly, just a few seconds per side -- lingering too long makes the base soggy instead of tender.
Keeps 3 days refrigerated.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
recipes.tagline: A moist, dense loaf built on very ripe, spotty bananas.
recipes.description: Overripe bananas mashed into a simple batter and baked into a moist loaf -- the best use for bananas too far gone to eat on their own.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 175C (350F) and grease a loaf pan.
Mash the bananas well in a large bowl, then stir in the melted butter.
Stir in the sugar, egg, and vanilla.
Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the mixture and stir in.
Fold in the flour just until combined.
steps.tip: Overmixing develops the gluten in the flour and makes the loaf tough instead of tender -- stop as soon as no dry flour is visible.

steps.text: Fold in walnuts, if using, then pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.

notes: The spottier and blacker the banana peel, the sweeter and more flavorful the bread -- avoid bananas that are still yellow and firm.
Keeps 4 days at room temperature wrapped; freezes well for up to 3 months.

image.caption: Let it cool completely before slicing, or it crumbles instead of cutting clean.

recipes.title: Chocolate Brownies
recipes.tagline: Dense, fudgy squares with a crackly top.
recipes.description: Melted chocolate and butter whisked with sugar and eggs until glossy, baked just until set -- the crackly top is the sign you got it right.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 175C (350F) and line an 8x8 in baking pan with parchment.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat and whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
steps.tip: Whisking hard at this stage is what gives brownies their shiny, crackly top -- do not skip it.

steps.text: Fold in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt just until no streaks remain.
Pour into the prepared pan, scatter with chocolate chips if using, and bake until the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone.
Cool in the pan before cutting into squares.

notes: Slight underbaking is what keeps brownies fudgy -- a toothpick should come out with a few moist crumbs, not clean.
Keeps 4 days in an airtight container at room temperature.

image.alt: Stack of fudgy chocolate brownies with a crackly top
image.caption: A few moist crumbs on the toothpick mean it's done, not underbaked.

recipes.title: Classic Apple Pie
recipes.tagline: Spiced apples baked in a flaky double crust until bubbling.
recipes.description: Sliced apples tossed with sugar and cinnamon, baked between two layers of buttery pastry until the filling bubbles through the vents.

items.note: peeled and sliced, a mix of tart and sweet

steps.text: Pulse the flour, salt, and sugar with the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs, then add ice water a tablespoon at a time until the dough just comes together.
Divide the dough in two, shape into discs, wrap, and refrigerate.
steps.tip: Cold butter and a short rest are what create flaky layers in the crust -- warm dough bakes up dense.

steps.text: Toss the apples with the sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Preheat the oven to 200C (400F). Roll out one disc of dough and line the pie dish.
Fill with the apple mixture, then roll out the second disc and place over the top, sealing and crimping the edges, and cut a few vents in the top.
Brush with the egg wash and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles through the vents.
Cool before slicing.
steps.tip: Slicing warm pie lets the filling run out -- letting it cool lets the juices set.

notes: A mix of tart apples (Granny Smith) and sweeter ones (Honeycrisp) gives the best balance of flavor and texture.
Cover the edges with foil partway through baking if they brown too quickly.

image.alt: Slice of apple pie showing spiced apple filling and a flaky crust
image.caption: Letting it cool fully is what keeps a slice from collapsing.

recipes.title: New York Cheesecake
recipes.tagline: Dense, creamy cheesecake baked over a buttery graham crust.
recipes.description: A thick cream cheese filling baked slowly in a water bath until just set, over a graham cracker crust -- rich, dense, and worth the wait for it to chill.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 160C (325F). Combine the crushed graham crackers, melted butter, and sugar, and press into the base of the springform pan.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar together until smooth and free of lumps.
steps.tip: Lumps in cold cream cheese never fully smooth out once the eggs go in -- beat it alone first until completely smooth.

steps.text: Beat in the eggs one at a time on low speed, then the sour cream, vanilla, and flour, mixing just until combined.
Pour the filling over the crust. Wrap the outside of the pan in foil and place in a roasting pan with hot water reaching partway up the sides.
Bake until the edges are set but the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off the oven and let the cheesecake cool inside with the door ajar for an hour, then refrigerate until fully chilled.
steps.tip: Cooling gradually in the oven is what prevents the top from cracking -- a sudden temperature change is the main cause.

steps.text: Run a knife around the edge before releasing the springform ring.

notes: A water bath insulates the cheesecake from direct heat, which is what keeps the texture creamy instead of curdled.
Keeps 5 days refrigerated.

recipes.title: Mixed Berry Smoothie
recipes.tagline: Frozen berries blended thick with yogurt and a touch of honey.
recipes.description: Frozen mixed berries blended with yogurt and a splash of milk until thick and cold -- no bananas required, so the berry flavor stays front and center.

steps.text: Combine the frozen berries, yogurt, milk, and honey in a blender.
Blend until smooth and thick, adding a splash more milk if it's too thick to pour.
steps.tip: Starting with less milk and adding more as needed keeps the smoothie thick instead of watery -- you can always loosen it, but you can't easily thicken it back up.

steps.text: Taste and adjust honey, then pour into glasses and serve immediately.

notes: Frozen berries make a colder, thicker smoothie than fresh -- no ice needed.
Swap the yogurt for a dairy-free version and the milk for a plant-based one to make it vegan.

recipes.title: Iced Coffee
recipes.tagline: Strong coffee cooled and poured over ice with milk.
recipes.description: Coffee brewed double-strength, cooled, and poured over ice with milk -- a far better result than pouring hot coffee straight over ice, which waters it down as it melts.

steps.text: Brew the coffee double the usual strength, then let it cool to room temperature or chill it.
steps.tip: Brewing it extra strong is what keeps the coffee from tasting watery once the ice starts to melt.

steps.text: Fill a tall glass with ice cubes.
Pour the cooled coffee over the ice.
Add milk and simple syrup to taste, and stir.

notes: Brew a batch ahead and refrigerate it specifically for iced coffee -- pouring hot coffee straight over ice dilutes it fast.
Cold brew concentrate works even better if you have the time to make it.

recipes.title: Fresh Lemonade
recipes.tagline: Squeezed lemons balanced with sugar syrup and cold water.
recipes.description: Fresh lemon juice mixed with a simple syrup and cold water -- brighter and less cloying than anything from a powdered mix or a bottle.

items.item: lemon slices and mint, to garnish

steps.text: Combine the sugar and water in a small saucepan and heat until the sugar dissolves completely, then let cool.
Juice the lemons, straining out the seeds.
Combine the lemon juice, sugar syrup, and cold water in a pitcher.
steps.tip: Making a syrup instead of stirring sugar directly into cold water is what dissolves it fully -- sugar stirred into cold liquid alone often stays grainy.

steps.text: Taste and adjust the balance of sweet and tart with more syrup or lemon juice.
Serve over ice, garnished with lemon slices and mint.

notes: Keeps 5 days refrigerated; the flavor is best within the first 2 days.
Adjust sweetness to taste -- lemons vary quite a bit in tartness.

recipes.title: Mango Lassi
recipes.tagline: Ripe mango blended with yogurt into a cold, creamy drink.
recipes.description: Sweet ripe mango blended with yogurt, a little sugar, and a pinch of cardamom -- a cooling drink that's just as at home with a spicy meal as on its own.

items.note: peeled and chopped, or 300g mango pulp

steps.text: Combine the mango, yogurt, milk, sugar, and cardamom in a blender.
Blend until completely smooth.
steps.tip: Very ripe, fragrant mangoes make all the difference here -- an underripe mango makes a thin, tart lassi that no amount of sugar fixes.

steps.text: Taste and adjust sugar, then blend briefly with ice cubes or pour over ice to serve.

notes: Frozen mango chunks work well out of season and give an even thicker, colder lassi.
Canned mango pulp (kesar or alphonso) is a good substitute when good fresh mangoes aren't available.

recipes.title: Hot Chocolate
recipes.tagline: Melted chocolate and milk whisked into a thick, rich drink.
recipes.description: Real chocolate melted directly into warm milk, not just cocoa powder stirred in -- the difference is a drink that's genuinely thick and rich, not just sweet.

steps.text: Warm the milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat until steaming but not boiling.
Remove from heat and whisk in the chopped chocolate until fully melted and smooth.
steps.tip: Melting the chocolate off the heat, whisking constantly, keeps it from seizing or scorching against the bottom of the pan.

steps.text: Return to low heat and whisk in the sugar, vanilla, and salt, warming through without boiling.
Pour into mugs and top with whipped cream or marshmallows, if using.

notes: Use the best dark chocolate you have -- this recipe has so few ingredients that the chocolate's quality is the whole drink.
Steaming, not boiling, the milk is what keeps it from developing a skin.

image.caption: Real chopped chocolate, not just cocoa powder, is what makes it thick.

recipes.title: Kala Bhuna
recipes.tagline: Beef slow-cooked in mustard oil and spices until deeply dark and glossy.
recipes.description: Chittagong's signature beef bhuna, cooked low and slow in caramelized onions and mustard oil with no added water, until the meat turns a deep blackish-brown and the oil separates out glossy at the edges.
equipment: Spice grinder or mortar and pestle

ingredientGroups.heading: For the bhuna masala (dry-roasted and ground)

steps.text: Marinate the beef with the ginger paste, garlic paste, turmeric, papaya paste if using, and salt. Set aside while you prepare the rest.
steps.tip: Papaya paste is the traditional tenderizer for the tougher, bone-in cuts bhuna is built on -- plain yogurt works if you can't find it.

steps.text: Dry roast the whole spices for the bhuna masala in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind to a fine powder.
steps.tip: Toasting the spices before grinding is what gives bhuna masala its deep, almost smoky aroma -- do not skip this even though the beef still has hours left to cook.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions over medium heat until deeply golden and starting to caramelize.
Add the bay leaves, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves, and cook until fragrant.
Add the marinated beef and sear on high heat until browned on all sides.
Stir in the red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder, and cook until the oil starts to separate from the spice paste.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, without adding any water.
steps.tip: This is the defining trait of bhuna cooking -- no added water. The dish simmers in its own released juices and rendered fat, which is what concentrates the flavor and eventually turns the beef dark.

steps.text: Once the beef is tender and the liquid has mostly cooked off, uncover, raise the heat slightly, and stir frequently until the mixture turns a deep blackish-brown and the oil visibly separates and pools at the edges.
steps.tip: This final dry-roasting stage is what "kala" (black) refers to -- the color comes from slow caramelization, not from burning, so keep the heat moderate and stir often.

steps.text: Stir in the ground bhuna masala and the slit green chilies, and cook a few minutes more to let the aroma bloom.
Taste and adjust salt, then garnish with crispy fried onions and serve.

notes: Traditionally made with beef leg or shank on the bone -- the collagen is part of what makes the sauce glossy and rich after hours of slow cooking.
Kala bhuna keeps and even improves for a day or two refrigerated; the flavor deepens as it sits.

image.alt: Bowl of dark, glossy Bangladeshi kala bhuna beef curry
image.caption: The deep blackish-brown color and glossy separated oil are the whole point.
